## Kyoto Spring Trip Snapshot
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/map.svg

A relaxed 4-day Kyoto plan for **2 adults** from **2026-04-10 to 2026-04-13** with **public transit only**, **one under-4-star hotel**, and a **food budget capped at 12,000 JPY/day**.
I’ve kept each day to **3 major activities max** and centered the trip on **temples, food markets, one easy hike, and a tea ceremony**.

## 4-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Budget Fit
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar.svg

| Day | Focus | Major activities | Food plan | Transit style | Estimated cost for 2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Apr 10 | Gion + tea ceremony | Arrive, check in, Yasaka Shrine / Gion stroll, tea ceremony | Light lunch + kaiseki-style dinner or set meal | Subway + bus + walking | 18,000–28,000 JPY |
| Apr 11 | Eastern Kyoto temples | Kiyomizu-dera, Sannenzaka/Ninenzaka, Kodai-ji or Chion-in | Temple-area breakfast, market lunch, casual dinner | Bus + walking | 16,000–26,000 JPY |
| Apr 12 | Market day + easy hike | Nishiki Market, Fushimi Inari easy partial hike, sake district walk | Market snacks + bowl lunch + izakaya-style dinner | Train + walking | 15,000–24,000 JPY |
| Apr 13 | Arashiyama + departure | Bamboo Grove, Tenryu-ji, easy riverside walk or short hill trail | Early breakfast, lunch in Arashiyama, airport/station snack | Train + walking | 16,000–27,000 JPY |

### Day 1: Gion Arrival and Tea Ceremony
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg

- **Morning:** Arrive in Kyoto, store luggage if needed, and check in to a **3-star or 3.5-star hotel** near Kyoto Station, Gion, or Karasuma for easy transit.
- **Afternoon:** Walk the **Gion** area and visit **Yasaka Shrine**; keep this as a light first day with plenty of café breaks.
- **Evening:** Book a **tea ceremony** in Gion or Higashiyama, then finish with an early dinner nearby.
- **Food:** Stay under the limit with a lunch set, tea ceremony sweets, and a dinner around **4,000–5,500 JPY per person**.

### Day 2: Eastern Kyoto Temples
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg

- **Morning:** Start early at **Kiyomizu-dera** to avoid crowds and heat.
- **Afternoon:** Wander **Sannenzaka/Ninenzaka** and choose one more temple stop such as **Kodai-ji** or **Chion-in**.
- **Evening:** Return to a calm neighborhood for dinner; keep the pace slow and skip extra sightseeing.
- **Food:** Use a temple-area breakfast, a market lunch, and a simple dinner to stay within **12,000 JPY/day for 2**.

### Day 3: Nishiki Market and Easy Fushimi Inari Hike
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/signpost-split.svg

- **Morning:** Explore **Nishiki Market** and sample small bites rather than a full sit-down meal.
Media: Alt=Morning:** Explore **Nishiki Market** and sample small bites rather than a full sit-down meal, Kyoto, Japan
- **Afternoon:** Take the train to **Fushimi Inari Taisha** and do an **easy partial hike**: the lower shrine area plus the first scenic section of torii gates is enough for a relaxed day.
- **Evening:** Walk the nearby **Fushimi sake district** or head back for an early dinner.
- **Food:** Market snacks, noodle/rice bowl lunch, and a modest dinner should keep you under budget.

### Day 4: Arashiyama and Departure Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg

- **Morning:** Take the train to **Arashiyama** and visit the **Bamboo Grove** early.
- **Afternoon:** See **Tenryu-ji** and do a gentle riverside walk or a short scenic stroll rather than adding more temples.
- **Evening:** Pick up snacks for departure and head to your next stop or back to the airport/rail hub.
- **Food:** Keep the day light with breakfast, lunch in Arashiyama, and a station snack to stay within the cap.

## Hotel and Transit Choice
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg

**Best fit:** a **3-star or 3.5-star hotel** near **Kyoto Station** or **Karasuma**.
Why this works:
- Easy access to JR, subway, and buses
- Good for a relaxed pace with fewer transfers
- Usually better value than staying inside the most tourist-heavy temple zones

**Transit plan:** use **IC card + JR/subway/bus** only; avoid taxis to protect the budget.

## Packing Checklist for Kyoto in April
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/briefcase.svg

- Lightweight jacket or cardigan for cool mornings and evenings
- Comfortable walking shoes with good grip
- Compact umbrella or rain shell
- Socks you can easily remove for temple visits
- Small day bag
- Portable phone charger
- Reusable water bottle
- Cash in yen for markets, shrines, and small shops
- Easy-to-remove layers for changing temperatures
- Modest outfit option for tea ceremony and temple etiquette
- Basic toiletries and any medication
- Transit card wallet or slim card holder

## Budget Check for the Trip
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/currency-rupee.svg

- **Hotel:** target **12,000–20,000 JPY/night** for a 3-star or 3.5-star property, or roughly **48,000–80,000 JPY total**
- **Food:** cap at **12,000 JPY/day** = **48,000 JPY total**
- **Local transit + admissions + tea ceremony:** roughly **25,000–45,000 JPY total**
- **Total estimated local trip cost:** about **121,000–173,000 JPY** for 2 adults, well within your **$2,800** budget excluding international flights
